Take-home Exercise 2: Technical Report

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

Recorded violence in Myanmar, January 2021–September 2025

Author

Davin Cuaso

Published

3 October 2026

Modified

6 October 2026

Submission hub · Ten-slide executive summary · Project source

1 Overview

Myanmar’s recorded conflict events are uneven in both space and time. A national total can show whether recorded activity rose or fell, but it cannot show whether neighbouring townships formed a local concentration or whether that concentration persisted. This report studies those questions with the supplied Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED) extract and the Myanmar Information Management Unit (MIMU) v9.4 township boundaries.

The study covers 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025. The spatial unit is the township and the temporal unit is the calendar month. The main measure is the number of recorded events. Reported fatalities are analysed separately because event frequency and severity are not interchangeable. Neither measure is adjusted for population, land area, road access, media access or reporting coverage.

The analysis has three layers. First, descriptive summaries establish what is in the supplied data. Second, Local Moran’s I and Getis-Ord Gi* test whether accumulated township totals form local clusters or spatial outliers. Third, an emerging hot spot analysis follows monthly local Gi* scores to identify how those patterns changed through time. Sensitivity checks examine coordinate precision and an alternative neighbour definition. A final extension measures movement in the event-weighted geographical centre.

The exercise brief contains two references to passenger trips and hexagons that do not match its Myanmar conflict task. I therefore follow the stated Myanmar objective, use townships as the geographical unit, and document that interpretation here rather than silently changing the problem.

2 Objectives

This report has five objectives:

  1. prepare a reproducible township-month dataset from the supplied ACLED extract and official MIMU boundaries;
  2. describe the spatial and temporal distribution of retained violence records and reported fatalities;
  3. identify statistically unusual local clusters and outliers with Local Moran’s I and Gi*;
  4. examine whether local hot and cold patterns persisted, intensified, diminished or changed category during the 57-month period; and
  5. test how much the main hotspot result depends on coordinate precision and the spatial-weights definition.

These objectives lead to four practical questions. Where was recorded violence concentrated? Which townships differed from their neighbours? Did the local pattern change over time? Which conclusions remain stable when plausible analytical choices are changed?

3 Getting started

3.1 R packages

The analysis uses pacman::p_load() so that all required packages are checked and attached in one call. This also keeps the package list visible at the start of the workflow.

Show the R code 
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}

pacman::p_load(sf, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, spdep,
               Kendall, knitr, scales)
Show the R code 
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Package = c("sf", "dplyr / tidyr", "spdep", "Kendall", "ggplot2 / scales", "knitr"),
  Purpose = c(
    "Import, validate, project and join spatial features",
    "Filter records, aggregate events and complete the township-month cube",
    "Build neighbours and run Local Moran and Gi* permutation tests",
    "Run the Mann-Kendall trend test on monthly Gi* scores",
    "Draw statistical maps, time-series plots and sensitivity figures",
    "Present audit tables and calculated results in the report"
  )
), col.names = c("Package", "Role in the analysis"))
Package Role in the analysis
sf Import, validate, project and join spatial features
dplyr / tidyr Filter records, aggregate events and complete the township-month cube
spdep Build neighbours and run Local Moran and Gi* permutation tests
Kendall Run the Mann-Kendall trend test on monthly Gi* scores
ggplot2 / scales Draw statistical maps, time-series plots and sensitivity figures
knitr Present audit tables and calculated results in the report

3.2 Data sources

Two supplied datasets enter the analysis. The raw ACLED file remains private because redistribution may be restricted; the derived non-sensitive outputs and code are stored with the project.

Show the R code 
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Data = c("ACLED course extract", "MIMU township boundaries v9.4"),
  Format = c("CSV", "GeoJSON"),
  Coverage = c("87,109 rows, 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025", "330 township polygons"),
  Fields_used = c(
    "event ID, date, event type, fatalities, longitude, latitude, coordinate precision",
    "township code and name, district, state or region, polygon geometry"
  ),
  Role = c("Recorded conflict events and reported fatalities", "Aggregation units and spatial neighbours")
), col.names = c("Dataset", "Format", "Coverage", "Main fields", "Use"))
Dataset Format Coverage Main fields Use
ACLED course extract CSV 87,109 rows, 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025 event ID, date, event type, fatalities, longitude, latitude, coordinate precision Recorded conflict events and reported fatalities
MIMU township boundaries v9.4 GeoJSON 330 township polygons township code and name, district, state or region, polygon geometry Aggregation units and spatial neighbours

The event ID is the duplicate check. event_date supplies the month. event_type defines the analytical scope. fatalities is kept as a separate outcome. Longitude, latitude and geo_precision determine whether a record is suitable for a township-level join. TS_PCODE, rather than a place-name string, is the stable key after the spatial join.

3.3 Importing and inspecting the files

The boundary file is imported with st_read(). The event file is read with UTF-8 BOM handling because course extracts can contain a byte-order mark in the first field name. Assertions stop the workflow if the expected 330 polygons, v9.4 code or unique identifiers are absent.

Show the R code 
raw <- read.csv(
  "data/private/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM"
)

townships <- st_read(
  "data/boundaries/mimu-v9.4.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  arrange(TS_PCODE)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(raw$event_id_cnty))
stopifnot(nrow(townships) == 330)
stopifnot(all(townships$PCode_V == "9.4"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(townships$TS_PCODE))

4 Exploratory data analysis

4.1 Event composition

The source contains six ACLED event types. The three categories used in the analysis account for 54,004 raw rows before the country, precision and polygon-match checks. Strategic developments, protests and riots are not included in the core violence measure.

Show the R code 
event_types <- event_types[order(-event_types$Freq), ]
names(event_types) <- c("Event type", "Records")
knitr::kable(event_types, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
Event type Records
Explosions/Remote violence 22,925
Battles 21,121
Strategic developments 17,833
Protests 15,203
Violence against civilians 9,958
Riots 69

This first table is descriptive rather than a result of the spatial model. It shows why the report defines its scope explicitly: using every row would mix demonstrations, strategic developments and direct violence in one count, while using only battles would omit explosions and violence against civilians.

4.2 Record retention and data-quality checks

The audit below applies each filter in sequence. “Removed at this step” is the difference from the preceding row, not a count of all records with that feature in the untouched CSV.

Show the R code 
audit_display <- a$audit
audit_display$removed <- c(
  "Not applicable",
  fmt(head(audit_display$n, -1) - tail(audit_display$n, -1))
)
knitr::kable(
  audit_display,
  col.names = c("Stage", "Records retained", "Removed at this step"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
Stage Records retained Removed at this step
Source records 87,109 Not applicable
Within study dates 87,109 0
Myanmar country label 87,103 6
Three core violence event types 54,000 33,103
Coordinate precision 1 or 2 53,907 93
Valid coordinates 53,907 0
Exactly one township match 53,899 8

Six records carry an Indian Ocean country label, 33,103 fall outside the three selected event types, 93 have coordinate precision 3, and eight do not intersect exactly one township polygon. No additional record is lost to the coordinate-validity check. The final analytical set contains 53,899 events and 89,005 reported fatalities.

Quality check Count Response

These checks cover the fields needed for this study. They do not imply that every unused column in the raw CSV is complete. The eight unmatched records are not forced into the nearest township because doing so would create location precision that the source does not support.

4.3 Summary statistics

The completed dataset has 18,810 observations: 330 townships observed in each of 57 months. Counts are strongly right-skewed and zero-heavy. The median township-month has no retained event, while the maximum has 96. Reported fatalities are even sparser and have a maximum of 419 in one township-month.

Show the R code 
cb <- sf::st_drop_geometry(b)
descriptive <- rbind(
  data.frame(Unit = "Township-month", Measure = "Events", Min = min(cube$events),
             Median = median(cube$events), Mean = mean(cube$events), Max = max(cube$events)),
  data.frame(Unit = "Township-month", Measure = "Reported fatalities", Min = min(cube$fatalities),
             Median = median(cube$fatalities), Mean = mean(cube$fatalities), Max = max(cube$fatalities)),
  data.frame(Unit = "Township total", Measure = "Events", Min = min(cb$events),
             Median = median(cb$events), Mean = mean(cb$events), Max = max(cb$events)),
  data.frame(Unit = "Township total", Measure = "Reported fatalities", Min = min(cb$fatalities),
             Median = median(cb$fatalities), Mean = mean(cb$fatalities), Max = max(cb$fatalities))
)
knitr::kable(descriptive, digits = 1)
Unit Measure Min Median Mean Max
Township-month Events 0 0 2.9 96
Township-month Reported fatalities 0 0 4.7 419
Township total Events 0 79 163.3 1039
Township total Reported fatalities 0 81 269.7 1877

There are 9,533 zero-event township-months (50.7%) and 12,381 zero-fatality township-months (65.8%). A zero means no qualifying record was present for that township-month. It does not prove that no violence occurred or that reporting coverage was complete.

5 Data wrangling

5.1 Defining the analytical events

Three event types define the analytical scope: battles, explosions/remote violence, and violence against civilians. This is a consistent operational definition of the core violence series, rather than every record tagged as political violence. The decision excludes protests, riots and strategic developments, including any violence described within those excluded categories, so the result must not be read as a complete count of every form of political violence.

Coordinate precision 3 is too broad for a township analysis and is excluded. Precision 2 is retained because removing every approximate location would discard a substantial part of the record. A separate precision-1-only analysis checks this decision. ACLED coordinates commonly identify a named place rather than the exact incident site, and reported fatality totals have substantial measurement uncertainty. A zero is treated as zero reported fatalities, not proof that nobody died. See the ACLED codebook.

Show the R code 
events <- raw |>
  mutate(event_date = as.Date(event_date)) |>
  filter(
    event_date >= as.Date("2021-01-01"),
    event_date <= as.Date("2025-09-30"),
    country == "Myanmar",
    event_type %in% c(
      "Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence",
      "Violence against civilians"
    ),
    geo_precision %in% c(1, 2),
    is.finite(longitude), is.finite(latitude)
  )

5.2 Repairing geometry, projecting and joining

The boundary source is the official MIMU v9.4 layer. st_make_valid() repairs geometry before analysis. Both polygons and WGS84 event points are transformed to a regional Albers equal-area projection centred at 96°E, with standard parallels at 10°N and 28°N. A projected coordinate system is needed for centroid distances and the geographical-centre extension.

st_intersects() assigns a point only when it intersects exactly one township. This geometry join avoids silently equating differently spelled place names. It does not remove uncertainty in the original coordinates or reconcile historical boundary changes. The same v9.4 geography is used throughout the period.

Show the R code 
aea <- paste(
  "+proj=aea +lat_1=10 +lat_2=28 +lat_0=19",
  "+lon_0=96 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
)

townships <- townships |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(aea)

event_points <- events |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326,
           remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(townships))

matches <- st_intersects(event_points, townships)
events$TS_PCODE <- vapply(
  matches,
  function(i) if (length(i) == 1) townships$TS_PCODE[i] else NA_character_,
  character(1)
)
events <- events[lengths(matches) == 1, ]
Show the R code 
showfig("locator")

The labels provide orientation for the township maps below. They are not the analytical units: every local test is performed on the 330 townships. Large northern and eastern polygons occupy more map space than compact urban townships, so visible area should not be confused with recorded event totals.

5.3 Building the complete township-month cube

Events are grouped by township code and month before they are joined to a complete 330 by 57 grid. Filling the absent combinations only after source validation prevents an invalid or unmatched row from being mistaken for a genuine zero. The precise field counts precision-1 events and supports the later sensitivity check.

Show the R code 
counts <- events |>
  mutate(month = as.Date(format(event_date, "%Y-%m-01"))) |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE, month) |>
  summarise(
    events = n(),
    fatalities = sum(fatalities),
    precise = sum(geo_precision == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cube <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  month = seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2025-09-01"), by = "month"),
  TS_PCODE = townships$TS_PCODE
) |>
  left_join(counts, by = c("TS_PCODE", "month")) |>
  mutate(across(c(events, fatalities, precise), ~replace_na(.x, 0L))) |>
  arrange(month, TS_PCODE)

stopifnot(nrow(cube) == 330 * 57)
stopifnot(sum(cube$events) == nrow(events))

The exported cube contains events, fatalities and precise. January 2021 and September 2025 are both included, and assertions verify the cube size and retained event total before any spatial statistic is calculated.

6 Recorded distribution

6.1 National monthly pattern

Show the R code 
showfig("monthly")

November 2023 has the largest monthly event count, 1,466, followed by December 2023 with 1,449. November 2023 also has the highest reported fatality total, 2,477. Other fatality peaks do not follow the event series exactly. The two panels use separate vertical scales, so their heights cannot be compared directly. Annual totals also need care because 2025 contains only nine months.

6.2 State and region totals

The table below is descriptive and does not replace the township tests. It helps locate the broader share of recorded activity before the report moves to local neighbourhoods.

  summarise(events = sum(events), fatalities = sum(fatalities), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(events)) |>
  mutate(
    event_share = events / sum(events),
    fatality_share = fatalities / sum(fatalities)

  slice_head(n = 10)

state_display <- state_totals
state_display$event_share <- scales::percent(state_display$event_share, accuracy = 0.1)
state_display$fatality_share <- scales::percent(state_display$fatality_share, accuracy = 0.1)

6.3 Township totals

Show the R code 
showfig("distribution-events")

Monywa has the largest retained total, 1,039 events, followed by Kawkareik (946) and Myaing (934). The map shows substantial variation within states and regions. A large total does not by itself establish a spatial hot spot: the next tests ask whether the township’s local neighbourhood is unusually high relative to the study area. Polygon area is not proportional to event count, and larger townships can dominate the visual impression.

Show the R code 
showfig("distribution-fatalities")

Kale has the largest reported fatality total in the retained data (1,877), followed by Monywa (1,771) and Maungdaw (1,583). This ordering differs from the event-count ranking. The distinction supports keeping frequency and reported severity separate throughout the analysis. Differences may reflect incident severity, reporting and fatality estimation as well as underlying conflict conditions.

top_events <- cb |>

  arrange(desc(events)) |>

  mutate(Rank = row_number(), Measure = "Events", Value = events) |>

  select(TS, ST, fatalities) |>
  arrange(desc(fatalities)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(Rank = row_number(), Measure = "Reported fatalities", Value = fatalities) |>
  select(Rank, Measure, Township = TS, `State or region` = ST, Value)

7 Spatial assumptions and tests

7.1 Defining neighbours

Queen contiguity treats townships sharing an edge or vertex as neighbours. This fits a question about adjacent local concentrations without imposing a single distance across townships of very different sizes. Three isolated polygons receive a symmetric link to their nearest projected centroid; the added links are recorded below. The choice is an analytical connection, not a claim about roads or movement.

Show the R code 
queen_nb <- poly2nb(townships, queen = TRUE)

# After adding a symmetric nearest-centroid link for each isolate:
moran_weights <- nb2listw(queen_nb, style = "W")
gistar_weights <- nb2listw(include.self(queen_nb), style = "W")

Row standardisation makes each township’s outgoing neighbour weights sum to one for Local Moran’s I. Gi* includes the focal township because the statistic asks whether the value at the location and values around it are jointly high or low. The isolate repair is symmetric, so adding an artificial link in one direction also adds the reverse link.

Show the R code 
links <- read.csv("results/island-links.csv")
lookup <- setNames(b$TS,b$TS_PCODE)
links$from_name <- lookup[links$from]
links$to_name <- lookup[links$to]
knitr::kable(links)
from to from_name to_name
MMR011003 MMR011001 Chaungzon Mawlamyine
MMR012012 MMR012013 Munaung Ramree
MMR013032 MMR017016 Cocokyun Labutta

Local Moran’s I uses row-standardised neighbour weights without self. Gi* includes self. The main maps use raw accumulated counts: the question is the geography of recorded burden, rather than a residual after accounting for population or land area. Heavy tails can influence these tests, particularly fatalities. The precision and alternative-neighbour checks below assess two specific choices; they do not resolve all model uncertainty.

7.2 Null models and significance

localmoran_perm() and localG_perm() use 9,999 conditional permutations, a fixed seed of 6262026, two-sided tests, and sampling without repetition within a simulated neighbourhood. The focal observation remains fixed; values assigned to other neighbour positions are drawn from the remaining observations. Thus the null concerns exchangeability of the recorded values across locations under this neighbourhood structure. It does not model the reporting process or explain the causes of violence.

The code selects the two-sided rank permutation p-value, not the normal approximation or folded tail. Significant maps use strict p < 0.05; other townships are neutral grey. Separate Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted values are saved for each metric and test across 330 townships. The map threshold follows the brief; the adjusted counts show how much evidence survives a multiple-testing check. See the Local Moran documentation and Gi* documentation.

Show the R code 
local_moran <- localmoran_perm(
  x, moran_weights, nsim = 9999, iseed = 6262026,
  no_repeat_in_row = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided"
)

local_gistar <- localG_perm(
  x, gistar_weights, nsim = 9999, iseed = 6262026,
  no_repeat_in_row = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided"
)

Local Moran’s I and Gi* answer related but different questions. Local Moran combines the standardised focal value with the mean of neighbouring standardised values, so it can distinguish high–high and low–low clusters from high–low and low–high outliers. Gi* asks whether the focal location and its self-inclusive neighbourhood have an unusually high or low sum. Agreement strengthens the descriptive case for a local concentration, but neither statistic establishes its cause.

8 Local measures of spatial association

8.1 Event clusters and outliers

Show the R code 
showfig("lisa-events")

There are 36 high–high and 50 low–low townships, with three low–high outliers: Hlaingbwe, Seikphyu and Pyinoolwin. These outliers have below-average totals beside neighbourhoods with above-average totals. They are not automatically safe locations or data errors. No high–low outlier passes the selected threshold. The remaining 241 townships lack sufficient evidence for a local classification in this test; that does not establish spatial randomness.

8.2 Fatality clusters and outliers

Show the R code 
showfig("lisa-fatalities")

The fatality analysis identifies 39 high–high, 64 low–low and four low–high townships. Its larger high–high group shows that local concentrations of reported fatalities extend beyond the event-count classification. This is a comparison of recorded burdens, not a test that one region is inherently more dangerous per resident. Fatality uncertainty and a few severe incidents can have substantial influence on the result.

8.3 Gi* hot spots and cold spots

Show the R code 
showfig("hotspot-events")

Gi* identifies 38 event hot spots and 50 cold spots. Eighteen of the hot spots are in Sagaing, seven in Mandalay and six in Magway. Kayin and Tanintharyi each contain three, and Bago (East) contains one. The concentration is therefore not confined to one administrative region. A cold spot is low relative to the national recorded distribution and its selected neighbourhood; it does not imply no incidents or low humanitarian need.

Show the R code 
showfig("hotspot-fatalities")

The fatality map identifies 43 hot spots and 65 cold spots. Sagaing contains 22 fatality hot spots and Magway seven; Chin contains four, although it contains none of the event hot spots under this specification. This difference would be lost if the analysis relied only on incident frequency. The maps are useful for identifying places for further review, but their significance is conditional on the chosen geography and measurement process.

Show the R code 
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Measure=c("Events: Local Moran", "Fatalities: Local Moran", "Events: Gi*", "Fatalities: Gi*"),
  Unadjusted=c(sum(se$moran_p<.05),sum(sf$moran_p<.05),sum(se$gi_p<.05),sum(sf$gi_p<.05)),
  BH_adjusted=c(sum(se$moran_q<.05),sum(sf$moran_q<.05),sum(se$gi_q<.05),sum(sf$gi_q<.05))
))
Measure Unadjusted BH_adjusted
Events: Local Moran 89 52
Fatalities: Local Moran 107 74
Events: Gi* 88 57
Fatalities: Gi* 108 73

9 Emerging hot spot analysis

9.1 A spatial and temporal neighbourhood

For each township-month, the neighbourhood includes the township and its queen neighbours in the current month and the preceding month. January 2021 has no preceding observation and therefore uses only its current slice. Binary weights identify included bins. Gi* is standardised against the full 18,810-bin cube, rather than separately against each month. This answers whether a neighbourhood-period is high or low relative to the entire study period. General national changes can therefore contribute to apparent local trends.

The implementation constructs an explicit space-time neighbour list and calls localG_perm() with 999 conditional permutations. The resulting local statistic uses both spatial and temporal neighbours. The null redistributes values among non-focal bins across the cube. It does not preserve national monthly totals, seasonality or serial correlation. The results are exploratory under that exchangeability assumption.

Show the R code 
for (t in seq_len(n_months)) {
  for (i in seq_len(n_townships)) {
    spatial_ids <- sort(unique(c(i, queen_nb[[i]])))
    current <- (t - 1L) * n_townships + spatial_ids
    previous <- if (t > 1) (t - 2L) * n_townships + spatial_ids else integer()
    spacetime_nb[[(t - 1L) * n_townships + i]] <-
      as.integer(sort(c(current, previous)))
  }
}

spacetime_weights <- nb2listw(spacetime_nb, style = "B")
monthly_gistar <- localG_perm(
  cube[[metric]], spacetime_weights,
  nsim = 999, iseed = 6262026,
  no_repeat_in_row = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided"
)

The Gi* standard scores are ordered by month before Kendall::MannKendall() is applied to each township. Positive tau indicates increasing scores; negative tau indicates decreasing scores. A Sen slope, calculated from all pairwise score changes, reports the median change in Gi* units per year. It describes a rate of change in the standardised spatial statistic, not a growth rate in violence.

For each township, the classification function receives the 57 ordered Gi* scores, their permutation p-values, Kendall’s tau and the trend p-value. It counts significant hot and cold months, inspects the final-month status, measures the uninterrupted run at the end, and then applies the category rules in a fixed order. Keeping this logic in a separate function makes the decision path auditable and prevents map styling from changing the classification.

9.2 Classification and the map filter

The classification code combines significant monthly bins with the final month and the Gi* trend. A new pattern appears only at the endpoint; consecutive patterns have a final uninterrupted run. At least 52 of 57 significant months are needed for the 90% persistence rule. Trend direction separates intensifying and diminishing histories; historical patterns no longer qualify in the final month. Intermittent final-period patterns are sporadic when no opposite-type bin occurred, and oscillating when one did. Unclassified histories remain neutral. New and consecutive rules take precedence where rules overlap. The Esri definitions guide these timing rules, but this R implementation is not claimed to reproduce ArcGIS software output.

The main EHSA maps require a classified history and Mann–Kendall p < 0.05, matching the chapter-style significant-trend display. Full-history maps are retained separately because persistent hot or cold patterns may have no significant trend. A single trend p-value must not be confused with the monthly bin tests.

Show the R code 
showfig("ehsa-significant-events")

66 townships have both a recognised event history and a significant trend. This filter is narrower than the complete history map. In the complete classification, oscillating hot spots number 26 and sporadic hot spots 9. An oscillating label means the sequence includes significant low as well as high local values; it does not mean conflict itself switched off and on. Because the reference distribution spans the whole study period, a low early month can contribute to that label.

Show the R code 
showfig("ehsa-significant-fatalities")

63 townships pass both conditions for fatalities. The complete fatality histories include 9 oscillating and 4 sporadic hot spots. Their smaller numbers relative to events reflect a different and more uneven variable. They should not be interpreted as independent confirmation of a trend in conflict mortality: the fatality totals remain reports attached to the same underlying events.

Show the R code 
showfig("trajectories")

Salingyi has 48 significant hot months, Myaing and Singu 47 each, and Yesagyo 46. None reaches the 52-month persistence threshold. Wetlet has 44 hot months yet is classified as no pattern detected because its endpoint and earlier history do not satisfy a named rule. That example is why the trajectory and hot-month count should accompany the map. “No pattern detected” is not equivalent to no sustained burden.

9.3 Multiplicity and time dependence

BH adjustment is also applied across all 18,810 bin p-values, separately for each measure. Reclassifying those bins changes 66 event histories and 95 fatality histories. With the adjusted fatality bins, all 330 townships have no classified pattern. This is a stringent check with limited permutation resolution; it is not evidence that no pattern exists.

Mann–Kendall’s usual p-value does not adjust for serial dependence. The overlapping two-month neighbourhood creates dependence by design, and real conflict series may be autocorrelated too. The unadjusted trend maps should therefore be treated as screening results. The output also includes BH-adjusted trend p-values, but BH does not repair serial dependence. No causal or predictive claim is made from these trend tests.

10 Robustness of the event hot spots

Show the R code 
showfig("robustness")

Of the 38 baseline event hot spots, 35 remain hot when only precision-1 events are counted and 28 remain hot with a symmetric four-nearest-neighbour graph. Twenty-seven pass both checks. The other 11 baseline hot spots are sensitive to at least one choice. Retention is not a probability of correctness: the precision-only subset changes the reporting composition, and nearest-centroid links change which townships are compared. The shared 27 provide a more defensible starting set for local review than the unqualified baseline map.

11 Extension: movement in the geographical centre

The additional question is whether recorded violence shifted geographically even when individual hotspot labels were unstable. For each year, I calculate the event-weighted average of township polygon centroids. Only January–September is used in every year, so the 2025 endpoint has the same calendar coverage as earlier years. Each month contributes its event count and its weighted coordinate sums.

To assess sensitivity to the months observed, I resample the nine whole monthly spatial fields within each year, with replacement, 1,999 times. Resampling a month preserves its cross-township distribution. The 2021 and 2025 samples are independent in this sensitivity calculation. This assumes the nine months are exchangeable; seasonality and serial dependence limit that assumption. The percentile interval is therefore a month-resampling sensitivity range, not an uncertainty interval for unreported violence.

Show the R code 
showfig("centre-shift")

The 2025 centre lies about 116 km from the 2021 centre: approximately 114 km south and 24 km west in the study projection. The resampled displacement range is 82–164 km. This indicates a change in the spatial balance of recorded events, not a moving front or a newly dangerous point. The centre can fall in a township with few events, especially when activity is split among several distant concentrations. The result complements the hotspot maps by summarising a broad geographical shift that a final categorical label cannot express.

12 Implications and limitations

The results support two levels of review. The 27 event hot spots that survive both checks are candidates for closer assessment of sustained local needs. Townships whose labels change with the assumptions need additional location validation before relying on their classification. Fatality concentrations provide a separate reason to investigate severity, including places outside the event-frequency hotspot set.

These are historical screening maps through September 2025. They cannot locate people currently at risk, recommend travel routes, or determine operational deployments. Any peace-building or humanitarian use would need current local knowledge, access information and needs assessments. Low recorded counts should never by themselves justify withdrawing assistance: under-reporting, displacement and inaccessible areas can all affect what enters the dataset.

Several boundaries remain unresolved. Township aggregation hides within-township variation; changing the unit would change the results. Static v9.4 boundaries impose one geography across the full period. Raw counts combine exposure, population, area and reporting intensity. No independent reporting-coverage series or suitable monthly population denominator is available here. Finally, significance depends on the neighbourhood, null model, permutation resolution and temporal assumptions; the robustness checks address only selected parts of that uncertainty.

13 Conclusion

The analysis reduces 87,109 source rows to 53,899 events that meet the stated date, country, event-type, coordinate-precision and polygon-match rules. That reduction is substantial, but it is documented step by step and every retained event belongs to exactly one of the 330 MIMU townships. Completing all 57 months for every township gives a consistent base for the temporal analysis and makes the meaning of each inserted zero explicit.

The descriptive results show that frequency and reported severity have related but different geographies. Monywa records the most retained events, while Kale records the largest reported fatality total. Sagaing accounts for 23.4% of retained events and 31.0% of reported fatalities, yet the township maps show that the pattern is not uniform within the region. These findings justify keeping events and fatalities as separate outcomes instead of combining them into a single conflict score.

The local tests provide evidence of spatial concentration under the selected queen-neighbour structure. Local Moran’s I identifies 36 high–high event townships and 39 high–high fatality townships. Gi* identifies 38 event hot spots and 43 fatality hot spots. The overlap is informative, but the methods are not interchangeable: Local Moran can identify spatial outliers, while Gi* measures a high or low self-inclusive neighbourhood sum. The multiple-testing summaries and neutral categories are therefore as important as the coloured clusters.

The emerging hot spot analysis adds a temporal qualification. Some townships have many significant hot months without satisfying a named endpoint rule, and the classifications are sensitive to correction across 18,810 monthly tests. The result is best read as a screening map of histories that deserve closer examination, not as proof that a township followed a fixed conflict trajectory. The separate trajectory plots and hot-month counts prevent the final category from hiding that detail.

The strongest practical conclusion comes from the sensitivity analysis. Twenty-seven of the 38 baseline event hot spots remain hot under both a precision-1-only count and a symmetric four-nearest-neighbour graph. Those 27 townships form the most stable set for further local review. The remaining baseline hot spots should be treated more cautiously because their labels depend on at least one reasonable analytical choice. The geographical-centre extension adds a broader observation: the event-weighted centre moved about 116 km between comparable January–September windows in 2021 and 2025. That shift describes the changing balance of recorded activity; it does not trace a front line or forecast future risk.

Taken together, the evidence supports a focused but cautious reading. Recorded violence was spatially concentrated, the geography of event frequency did not perfectly match the geography of reported fatalities, and several local concentrations persisted across alternative specifications. At the same time, reporting conditions, denominator data, boundary choice and temporal dependence prevent causal or population-risk claims. The report therefore identifies places and patterns for follow-up rather than declaring definitive levels of danger.

14 Reproducibility and code walkthrough

Run Rscript setup.R once to install missing dependencies, place the supplied CSV under data/private/, then run quarto render Take-home_Ex02-report.qmd. The default render executes the full pipeline and redraws all figures. quarto render Executive-summary.qmd builds the slides from those outputs. The source CSV and excluded-record audit are omitted from the shareable ZIP and ignored by Git; the README explains how to restore the local input.

R/analysis.R handles validation, joins, the complete cube, local statistics and space-time permutations. R/classify.R isolates the timing rules so they can be inspected without rerunning the permutations. R/reclassify.R derives the history labels and Sen slopes from saved bins. R/figures.R draws the maps, runs the geographical-centre extension, and exports its results. The code below is the actual implementation used by this page.

R/analysis.R 
pacman::p_load(sf, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, spdep, Kendall, knitr, scales)
set.seed(6262026)
raw_path <- Sys.getenv("ACLED_CSV", unset = "data/private/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv")
if (!file.exists(raw_path)) stop("ACLED CSV not found. Restore data/private/ or set ACLED_CSV.")
raw <- read.csv(raw_path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(raw$event_id_cnty))
raw$event_date <- as.Date(raw$event_date)
write.csv(as.data.frame(table(raw$event_type)), "results/event-types.csv", row.names = FALSE)
b <- st_read("data/boundaries/mimu-v9.4.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
    arrange(TS_PCODE)
stopifnot(nrow(b) == 330, all(b$PCode_V == "9.4"), !anyDuplicated(b$TS_PCODE))
b <- st_transform(st_make_valid(b), "+proj=aea +lat_1=10 +lat_2=28 +lat_0=19 +lon_0=96 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")
audit <- data.frame(stage = "Source records", n = nrow(raw))
add_audit <- function(x, label) {
    audit <<- rbind(audit, data.frame(stage = label, n = nrow(x)))
    x
}
e <- raw |>
    filter(event_date >= as.Date("2021-01-01"), event_date <= as.Date("2025-09-30")) |>
    add_audit("Within study dates")
e <- e |>
    filter(country == "Myanmar") |>
    add_audit("Myanmar country label")
e <- e |>
    filter(event_type %in% c("Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence", "Violence against civilians")) |>
    add_audit("Three core violence event types")
e <- e |>
    filter(geo_precision %in% c(1, 2)) |>
    add_audit("Coordinate precision 1 or 2")
e <- e |>
    filter(is.finite(longitude), is.finite(latitude), abs(longitude) <= 180, abs(latitude) <=
        90) |>
    add_audit("Valid coordinates")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(e$fatalities)), all(e$fatalities >= 0))
pts <- st_transform(st_as_sf(e, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE),
    st_crs(b))
matches <- st_intersects(pts, b)
e$join_n <- lengths(matches)
write.csv(e[e$join_n != 1, c("event_id_cnty", "event_date", "admin3", "longitude", "latitude",
    "geo_precision", "join_n")], "results/excluded-spatial-records.csv", row.names = FALSE)
e$TS_PCODE <- vapply(matches, function(z) if (length(z) == 1) b$TS_PCODE[z] else NA_character_,
    character(1))
e <- e |>
    filter(join_n == 1) |>
    add_audit("Exactly one township match")
e$month <- as.Date(format(e$event_date, "%Y-%m-01"))
write.csv(audit, "results/audit.csv", row.names = FALSE)
months <- seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2025-09-01"), by = "month")
# Absent recorded events become zero only after validating the source values.
counts <- e |>
    group_by(TS_PCODE, month) |>
    summarise(events = n(), fatalities = sum(fatalities), precise = sum(geo_precision ==
        1), .groups = "drop")
cube <- expand_grid(month = months, TS_PCODE = b$TS_PCODE) |>
    left_join(counts, by = c("TS_PCODE", "month")) |>
    mutate(across(c(events, fatalities, precise), ~replace_na(.x, 0L))) |>
    arrange(month, TS_PCODE)
stopifnot(nrow(cube) == 330 * 57, sum(cube$events) == nrow(e))
write.csv(cube, "results/township-month-cube.csv", row.names = FALSE)
totals <- cube |>
    group_by(TS_PCODE) |>
    summarise(across(c(events, fatalities, precise), sum), .groups = "drop")
b <- left_join(b, totals, by = "TS_PCODE")
# Queen neighbors include shared vertices. Isolates receive a symmetric nearest
# link.
nb <- poly2nb(b, queen = TRUE)
cent <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(b)))
iso <- which(card(nb) == 0)
links <- data.frame(from = character(), to = character())
for (i in iso) {
    d <- rowSums((cent - matrix(cent[i, ], nrow(b), 2, byrow = TRUE))^2)
    d[i] <- Inf
    j <- which.min(d)
    nb[[i]] <- as.integer(j)
    nb[[j]] <- sort(unique(as.integer(c(nb[[j]][nb[[j]] > 0], i))))
    links <- rbind(links, data.frame(from = b$TS_PCODE[i], to = b$TS_PCODE[j]))
}
write.csv(links, "results/island-links.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# Select the two-sided permutation column, not the folded (one-tail) column.
getp <- function(m) {
    k <- grep("Sim", colnames(m))
    k <- k[!grepl("folded", colnames(m)[k])]
    stopifnot(length(k) == 1)
    as.numeric(m[, k])
}
class_g <- function(z, p) ifelse(p < 0.05 & z > 0, "Hot spot", ifelse(p < 0.05 & z < 0,
    "Cold spot", "Not significant"))
static <- function(x, neighbors = nb) {
    w <- nb2listw(neighbors, style = "W")
    lm <- localmoran_perm(x, w, nsim = 9999, iseed = 6262026, no_repeat_in_row = TRUE,
        alternative = "two.sided")
    zz <- as.numeric(scale(x))
    lag <- lag.listw(w, zz)
    p <- getp(lm)
    cl <- ifelse(p < 0.05, ifelse(zz > 0, ifelse(lag > 0, "High–high", "High–low"),
        ifelse(lag > 0, "Low–high", "Low–low")), "Not significant")
    g <- localG_perm(x, nb2listw(include.self(neighbors), style = "W"), nsim = 9999, iseed = 6262026,
        no_repeat_in_row = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
    gp <- getp(attr(g, "internals"))
    data.frame(moran_I = lm[, 1], moran_p = p, moran_q = p.adjust(p, "BH"), lisa = cl,
        gi_z = as.numeric(g), gi_p = gp, gi_q = p.adjust(gp, "BH"), hotspot = class_g(as.numeric(g),
            gp))
}
for (metric in c("events", "fatalities")) {
    s <- static(b[[metric]])
    write.csv(cbind(st_drop_geometry(b)[, c("TS_PCODE", "TS", "ST")], s), paste0("results/static-",
        metric, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
# Space-time Gi*: current and previous month, including self and spatial neighbors.
# The full cube is the reference population. January has only its current slice.
n <- nrow(b)
nt <- length(months)
stnb <- vector("list", n * nt)
for (t in seq_len(nt)) for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    spatial <- sort(unique(c(i, nb[[i]])))
    v <- (t - 1L) * n + spatial
    if (t > 1)
        v <- c(v, (t - 2L) * n + spatial)
    stnb[[(t - 1L) * n + i]] <- as.integer(sort(v))
}
class(stnb) <- "nb"
attr(stnb, "region.id") <- as.character(seq_len(n * nt))
attr(stnb, "sym") <- FALSE
attr(stnb, "self.included") <- TRUE
stlw <- nb2listw(stnb, style = "B")
source("R/classify.R")

for (metric in c("events", "fatalities")) {
    message("Space-time permutations: ", metric)
    g <- localG_perm(cube[[metric]], stlw, nsim = 999, iseed = 6262026, no_repeat_in_row = TRUE,
        alternative = "two.sided")
    gp <- getp(attr(g, "internals"))
    z <- as.numeric(g)
    bins <- cbind(cube[, c("month", "TS_PCODE")], gi_z = z, p = gp, q = p.adjust(gp, "BH"))
    write.csv(bins, paste0("results/space-time-", metric, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    eh <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
        idx <- seq(i, n * nt, by = n)
        mk <- MannKendall(z[idx])
        tau <- as.numeric(mk$tau)
        mp <- as.numeric(mk$sl)
        data.frame(TS_PCODE = b$TS_PCODE[i], TS = b$TS[i], ST = b$ST[i], tau = tau, mk_p = mp,
            hot_months = sum(gp[idx] < 0.05 & z[idx] > 0), cold_months = sum(gp[idx] <
                0.05 & z[idx] < 0), classification = class_eh(z[idx], gp[idx], tau, mp),
            fdr_classification = class_eh(z[idx], bins$q[idx], tau, mp))
    }) |>
        bind_rows()
    eh$mk_q <- p.adjust(eh$mk_p, "BH")
    write.csv(eh, paste0("results/ehsa-", metric, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
source("R/reclassify.R")

knb <- make.sym.nb(knn2nb(knearneigh(cent, k = 4)))

R/classify.R 
# EHSA timing rules; new and consecutive histories take precedence over oscillating.
class_eh <- function(z, p, tau, mp) {
    hot <- p < 0.05 & z > 0
    cold <- p < 0.05 & z < 0
    N <- length(z)
    for (side in c("hot", "cold")) {
        a <- if (side == "hot")
            hot else cold
        opp <- if (side == "hot")
            cold else hot
        name <- if (side == "hot")
            "hot spot" else "cold spot"
        if (!a[N] && sum(a) >= 0.9 * N)
            return(paste("Historical", name))
        if (a[N]) {
            if (sum(a) == 1)
                return(paste("New", name))
            if (sum(a) >= 0.9 * N) {
                trend <- if (side == "hot")
                  tau else -tau
                return(paste(if (mp < 0.05) if (trend > 0) "Intensifying" else "Diminishing" else "Persistent",
                  name))
            }
            if (all(a[min(which(a)):N]))
                return(paste("Consecutive", name))
            if (any(opp))
                return(paste("Oscillating", name))
            return(paste("Sporadic", name))
        }
    }
    "No pattern detected"
}
R/reclassify.R 
# Reuse the already computed permutation results; no new random draws.
pacman::p_load(dplyr, Kendall)
source("R/classify.R")
for (metric in c("events", "fatalities")) {
    eh <- read.csv(paste0("results/ehsa-", metric, ".csv"))
    bins <- read.csv(paste0("results/space-time-", metric, ".csv"))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(eh))) {
        x <- bins[bins$TS_PCODE == eh$TS_PCODE[i], ]
        eh$classification[i] <- class_eh(x$gi_z, x$p, eh$tau[i], eh$mk_p[i])
        eh$fdr_classification[i] <- class_eh(x$gi_z, x$q, eh$tau[i], eh$mk_p[i])
        pairs <- combn(seq_len(nrow(x)), 2)
        eh$sen_z_per_year[i] <- 12 * median((x$gi_z[pairs[2, ]] - x$gi_z[pairs[1, ]])/(pairs[2,
            ] - pairs[1, ]))
    }
    write.csv(eh, paste0("results/ehsa-", metric, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

savep <- function(p, name, w = 10, h = 8) {
    p$labels$title <- paste(strwrap(p$labels$title, width = floor(w * 6.5)), collapse = "\n")
    p$labels$subtitle <- paste(strwrap(p$labels$subtitle, width = floor(w * 9)), collapse = "\n")
    p <- p + theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 9))
    ggsave(paste0("figures/", name, ".png"), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 180, bg = "white")
}

        `Low–high` = "#67a9cf", `Not significant` = "#e7e9ec")
    savep(base_map(d, "lisa", paste(label, "| Local Moran’s I"), "Two-sided permutation p < .05 • 9,999 permutations") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = pal), paste0("lisa-", metric), 7, 9)
    savep(base_map(d, "hotspot", paste(label, "| Gi*"), "Two-sided permutation p < .05 • self included") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Hot spot` = "#b2182b", `Cold spot` = "#2166ac",
            `Not significant` = "#e7e9ec")), paste0("hotspot-", metric), 7, 9)
    eh <- if (metric == "events")
        ee else ef
    d <- left_join(b, eh[, c("TS_PCODE", "classification", "tau", "mk_p")], by = "TS_PCODE")
    levels <- c("New hot spot", "Consecutive hot spot", "Intensifying hot spot", "Persistent hot spot",
        "Diminishing hot spot", "Sporadic hot spot", "Oscillating hot spot", "Historical hot spot",
        "New cold spot", "Consecutive cold spot", "Intensifying cold spot", "Persistent cold spot",
        "Diminishing cold spot", "Sporadic cold spot", "Oscillating cold spot", "Historical cold spot",
        "No pattern detected")
    colors <- c("#fdae61", "#f46d43", "#a50026", "#d73027", "#fdbf6f", "#e78ac3", "#8e0152",
        "#a6611a", "#abd9e9", "#74add1", "#053061", "#2166ac", "#92c5de", "#80cdc1", "#5e4fa2",
        "#4393c3", "#e7e9ec")
    savep(base_map(d, "classification", paste(label, "| emerging patterns"), "57 months • queen neighbours + previous month • bin p < .05") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(colors, levels)) + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)),
        paste0("ehsa-", metric), 8, 10)
    d$significant_class <- ifelse(d$mk_p < 0.05 & d$classification != "No pattern detected",
        d$classification, "No significant classified trend")
    savep(base_map(d, "significant_class", paste(label, "| EHSA with trend filter"), "Classified bin history and Mann–Kendall p < .05") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(setNames(colors, levels), `No significant classified trend` = "#e7e9ec")) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)), paste0("ehsa-significant-", metric), 8,
        10)
    d$trend <- ifelse(d$mk_p < 0.05, ifelse(d$tau > 0, "Increasing Gi*", "Decreasing Gi*"),
        "Not significant")
    savep(base_map(d, "trend", paste(label, "| Gi* trend"), "Mann–Kendall p < .05 • unadjusted for serial dependence") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Increasing Gi*` = "#b2182b", `Decreasing Gi*` = "#2166ac",
            `Not significant` = "#e7e9ec")), paste0("trend-", metric), 7, 9)
}
monthly <- cube |>
    group_by(month) |>
    summarise(events = sum(events), fatalities = sum(fatalities), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "measure", values_to = "count")
savep(ggplot(monthly, aes(month, count)) + geom_line(color = "#126b78", linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = "Recorded violence varies sharply across the study period", subtitle = "Monthly national totals • separate vertical scales",
        x = NULL, y = "Count", caption = cap), "monthly", 10, 6)
# Compare significant Gi* classifications across assumptions, including neutral
# townships.
rob$status <- ifelse(rob$baseline == "Hot spot" & rob$precise_only == "Hot spot" & rob$knn4 ==
    "Hot spot", "Hot in all three", ifelse(rob$baseline == "Hot spot", "Baseline hot: sensitive",
    "Other townships"))
d <- left_join(b, rob[, c("TS_PCODE", "status")], by = "TS_PCODE")
savep(base_map(d, "status", "Which event hot spots survive both checks?", "Precision-1-only records and symmetric 4-nearest-neighbour weights") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Hot in all three` = "#8c1738", `Baseline hot: sensitive` = "#f4a259",
        `Other townships` = "#e7e9ec")), "robustness", 7, 9)
# A separate geospatial extension: displacement of the event-weighted centre.  Use
# Jan–Sep in every year so that the partial 2025 year is comparable.
xy <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(b)))
coords <- data.frame(TS_PCODE = b$TS_PCODE, x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2])
mcent <- cube |>
    filter(as.integer(format(month, "%m")) <= 9) |>
    left_join(coords, by = "TS_PCODE") |>
    mutate(year = format(month, "%Y")) |>
    group_by(year, month) |>
    summarise(sx = sum(x * events), sy = sum(y * events), n = sum(events), .groups = "drop")
centres <- mcent |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(x = sum(sx)/sum(n), y = sum(sy)/sum(n), events = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
set.seed(6262026)
boot <- lapply(split(mcent, mcent$year), function(d) t(replicate(1999, {
    s <- d[sample(seq_len(nrow(d)), replace = TRUE), ]
    c(sum(s$sx)/sum(s$n), sum(s$sy)/sum(s$n))
})))
delta <- boot[["2025"]] - boot[["2021"]]
dist <- sqrt(rowSums(delta^2))/1000
actual <- as.numeric(centres[centres$year == "2025", c("x", "y")] - centres[centres$year ==
    "2021", c("x", "y")])
summary <- data.frame(dx_km = actual[1]/1000, dy_km = actual[2]/1000, distance_km = sqrt(sum(actual^2))/1000,
    boot_low = quantile(dist, 0.025), boot_high = quantile(dist, 0.975))
write.csv(summary, "results/centre-shift.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(centres, "results/annual-centres.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cloud <- bind_rows(lapply(names(boot), function(y) data.frame(year = y, x = boot[[y]][,
    1], y = boot[[y]][, 2])))
# Zoom to the centres so the annual displacement is visible at presentation size.
centres$label_x <- centres$x + c(45000, -70000, 65000, -70000, 40000)
centres$label_y <- centres$y + c(12000, 18000, -2000, -18000, -18000)
p <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = states, fill = "#f0f2f4", color = "#8794a0", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(data = cloud, aes(x, y, color = year), alpha = 0.08, size = 0.7) + geom_path(data = centres,
    aes(x, y), color = "#263746", arrow = arrow(length = grid::unit(0.12, "inches"))) +
    geom_point(data = centres, aes(x, y, color = year), size = 3) + geom_segment(data = centres,
    aes(x = x, y = y, xend = label_x, yend = label_y), color = "#52616b", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_label(data = centres, aes(label_x, label_y, label = year, color = year), fill = "white",
        size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) + annotate("segment", x = -1e+05, xend = -50000, y = 85000, yend = 85000,
    linewidth = 1) + annotate("text", x = -75000, y = 76000, label = "50 km", size = 3.5) +
    coord_sf(datum = NA, xlim = c(-130000, 135000), ylim = c(65000, 280000), expand = FALSE) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + labs(title = "The event-weighted centre moves south",
    subtitle = "Central Myanmar detail • January–September each year", color = "Year",
    caption = cap) + theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank())
savep(p, "centre-shift", 8, 8)
# Representative township trajectories make the EHSA labels inspectable.
top <- ee |>
    filter(hot_months > 0) |>
    arrange(desc(hot_months)) |>
    slice_head(n = 6)
st <- read.csv("results/space-time-events.csv")
st$month <- as.Date(st$month)
st <- st |>
    inner_join(top[, c("TS_PCODE", "TS", "classification")], by = "TS_PCODE") |>
    mutate(sig = ifelse(p < 0.05 & gi_z > 0, "Hot", ifelse(p < 0.05 & gi_z < 0, "Cold",
        "Not significant")))
savep(ggplot(st, aes(month, gi_z)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") + geom_line(color = "#8794a0") +
    geom_point(aes(color = sig), size = 1.1) + facet_wrap(~TS, ncol = 2) + scale_color_manual(values = c(Hot = "#b2182b",
    Cold = "#2166ac", `Not significant` = "#b6bec6")) + labs(title = "The six townships with the most hot months",
    subtitle = "Spatio-temporal Gi* • points use permutation significance, not a fixed Z cutoff",
    x = NULL, y = "Gi* standard score", color = NULL, caption = cap), "trajectories",
    11, 8)
message("Figures complete")

14.1 Full-history maps

These supplementary maps retain all recognised histories based on significant bins; they do not apply the extra Mann–Kendall filter used in the main EHSA maps.

Show the R code 
showfig("ehsa-events")

The complete map retains persistent cold histories that may be omitted by a trend-only display. It also shows why the end-of-series rule matters: a township can have many hot months without qualifying for a named endpoint pattern. The full CSV includes each township’s hot-month count, cold-month count and trend results for inspection.

Show the R code 
showfig("ehsa-fatalities")

These histories use the unadjusted bin threshold specified in the main method. Their sensitivity to multiple testing is substantial, as described above. They show where a possible pattern warrants examination, rather than providing a definitive classification of the underlying conflict process.
